reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) supports spray-coating, low friction/wear at room temperature under high load, and a tribocatalytic mechanism in ambient conditions for steel substrates. However, no evidence is provided for performance at elevated temperatures (up to 800 °C), on a CoCrFeNi substrate, or for the claimed suppression of high-temperature oxidation and adhesion, leaving the key premise of wide-temperature efficacy entirely unsupported.
premises: 2D (MoWNbTaV)0.2S2 nanoflakes can be spray-coated onto substrates
The coating provides low friction (COF ~0.076) and wear rate (~10^-9 mm3/Nm) under high contact pressure in ambient conditions
The low friction and wear are due to shear-induced tribocatalytic activity forming lubricious interfacial films
The tribocatalytic mechanism dissipates frictional stress and counters deleterious oxidation
These properties will persist from room temperature up to 800 °C on a CoCrFeNi substrate
